manifest.name: chart.setType
manifest.summary: Change how price is drawn on one chart.

manifest.name: chart.setTimeframe
manifest.summary: Change one chart's timeframe.
manifest.hints: Codes: 1, 5, 15, 30, 60 are minutes; D daily, W weekly, M monthly.

manifest.name: chart.setSymbol
manifest.summary: Show a different ticker on one chart. Widgets linked to the same color group follow, exactly as a manual symbol search does.

manifest.name: chart.setSession
manifest.summary: Show or hide pre/post-market (extended hours) on one chart.

manifest.name: chart.setScale
manifest.summary: Set one chart's price scale: linear (arithmetic), logarithmic, or percent.

manifest.name: chart.applyTheme
manifest.summary: Apply one of UCT's built-in chart color themes (canvas, candles, grid, text) to one chart.

manifest.name: chart.setBackground
manifest.summary: Set one chart's background to a single solid color.
manifest.hints: Pass a hex color like #f3efe4; translate plain color names to hex.

manifest.name: chart.setCandleColors
manifest.summary: Set one chart's up and/or down candle colors.
manifest.hints: Hex colors; pass null for a side that should not change.

manifest.name: volume.setState
manifest.summary: Show, hide, or remove one chart's built-in Volume pane.
manifest.hints: "hide volume" is hidden (stays in the legend); "remove volume" is removed (off the chart).

manifest.name: chart.setSetting
manifest.summary: Change one chart display setting from UCT's approved list (grid, crosshair, scale text, legend, watermark incl. opacity/position, labels, event/IPO markers, dark-pool levels, swing labels, prev-day lines, countdown, title, color mode, thin bars, inverted scale, gradient background, Volume pane colors/label/MA/bar style/height, Heikin Ashi, Chart IQ, position calculator defaults).
manifest.hints: value = true/false for on/off settings (crosshair.mode, header.legendMode and bgMode too); a hex color (#2962ff) for colors; a number in range. Allowed — crosshair.mode, header.legendMode: always|hold|off; textSize: 8|10|11|12|14|16|18|20|22|24|28|32|40; header.titleMode: ticker|company|both; candleColorMode: onecolor|netchange|openclose; swingLabels.sensitivity: low|medium|high; crosshair.width, prevDayLevels.high|low|close.width, volume.maLineWidth: 1|2|3|4; crosshair.style, prevDayLevels.high|low|close.style, volume.maLineStyle: solid|dashed|dotted; watermark.sizeScale: 0.5|0.75|1|1.25|1.5|2|2.5|3|4; watermark.weight: 300|400|500|600|700|800; bgMode: solid|gradient; volume.barStyle: columns|histogram; volume.paneHeightPct: 8–45 (whole); volume.maPeriod: 0–500 (whole); watermark.opacity|x|y: 0–1; positionCalc.accountSize: 0–1000000000; positionCalc.riskPct: 0–100. Any other setting (header info-row fields, volume plot style…): no op — say where it lives in Chart Settings.
manifest.shape: args {"setting": <one id from the list>, "value": …} — "turn the gradient off" = {"setting":"bgMode","value":"solid"}, "gradient on" = {"setting":"bgMode","value":"gradient"}, "hide the grid" = {"setting":"grid.visible","value":false}. Never invent a setting id (no "bgGradient.enabled", no "background.gradient"): an on/off wish for a setting not listed is unsupported.

manifest.name: chart.applyTemplate
manifest.summary: Apply one of the member's saved chart templates to ONE chart, exactly as clicking it does (Chart Settings → Templates, or right-click → Chart template): the chart takes the template's whole saved setup, its indicators included.
manifest.hints: template = a name from chartTemplates, exactly. For several charts ("all my charts"), one op per chart.

manifest.name: chart.resetDefaults
manifest.summary: Restore ONE chart's look to UCT's defaults (Chart Settings → Restore defaults): colours, markers, header, watermark and display settings. The chart's indicators are kept exactly as they are.
manifest.hints: target = the chart. Always shown as a proposal first.

manifest.name: chart.goToDate
manifest.summary: Scroll ONE chart so a past date is at its right edge — exactly the Time Navigator date box. A view change only: every bar stays on the chart (it is not a replay), nothing is saved; Undo scrolls back.
manifest.hints: date = YYYY-MM-DD. "As it looked on <date>" = this (say in the reply that later bars are still there, just scrolled off to the right).

manifest.name: chart.replay
manifest.summary: Replay Mode (Tools → Replay): hide every bar after a date on the linked charts, as if it were that day — or exit replay (date null). A view only: nothing is saved; Undo clears it (or restores the previous cutoff).
manifest.hints: date = YYYY-MM-DD (or the member's date word: "last friday", "oct 15") for the cutoff; null = exit replay. "As of <date>" / "replay from <date>" / "go back to <date> and hide what came after" = this; "scroll to <date>" with every bar kept = chart.goToDate.
manifest.shape: {"date":"YYYY-MM-DD"} to replay from a date; {"date":null} to EXIT replay ("exit replay", "leave replay", "replay off", "show every bar again") — the JSON null, never the word "null" and never an "exit" or "enabled" key.

manifest.name: chart.compare
manifest.summary: Overlay other symbols on ONE chart (Tools → Compare Symbols): add tickers, remove some, or clear all comparisons.
manifest.hints: add = tickers to overlay, uppercase ([] for none); remove = tickers to take off ([] for none); clear = true to remove every comparison. "Compare NVDA against QQQ on this chart" = target the NVDA chart, add [QQQ].

manifest.name: chart.addCustomTimeframe
manifest.summary: Add a custom timeframe (e.g. 45 minutes, 2 hours, 3 days) to ONE chart's timeframe menu, exactly like the menu's Custom interval, and optionally switch the chart to it.
manifest.hints: unit = minutes | hours | days | weeks | months; count = how many (45 for 45 minutes); switch = true to show the chart on it now (the usual case), false to only add it to the menu.

manifest.name: widget.add
manifest.summary: Add ONE widget of a given type to the Charts workspace, placed automatically in empty space. Use one op per widget.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the workspace entry. "as" NAMES THE NEW WIDGET: if any later op in this plan changes the new widget (a new chart's symbol, timeframe, …), set "as" to a short unique name (new1, new2, …) and use exactly that name as those ops' target — a later op may not target a new widget whose "as" is null. Otherwise "as" is null. Example: "add 2 charts on SPY and QQQ" → widget.add{type:chart, as:"new1"}, widget.add{type:chart, as:"new2"}, chart.setSymbol@new1{SPY}, chart.setSymbol@new2{QQQ}. Never drop a ticker the member named ("open a QQQ chart" needs its chart.setSymbol). Types: chart (Chart), watchlist (Watchlist), themes (Theme Tracker), scanner (Scanner), fundamentals (Fundamentals), breadth (Breadth), aisearch (AI Search), news (News & Catalysts), notebook (Notebook), profile (Stock Profile), alerts (Alerts), calendar (UCT Terminal), optionsflow (Options Flow), nhnl (New Highs / Lows), nhnlPulse (H/L Pulse), volumescan (Volume Surge), scatter (Market Map).

manifest.name: widget.addCharts
manifest.summary: Add one NEW chart per symbol of an ordered list (tickers, a screen's results, or a saved watchlist), placed together in empty space. Existing widgets are never changed.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the workspace entry. symbols = the tickers, uppercase, OR {from, top} to chart a source's stocks in its order: from = the ref of a saved watchlist (its stocks, read fresh in its saved order when they apply), the "as" of a screener.run / screener.runSaved op in this request, or "lastScreen" for the last screen run here; top = how many charts (required, at most 12). timeframe: 1|5|15|30|60 minutes, D, W, M, or null to keep the default. chart_type: candles|hollow|bars|hlc|line|area or null. exact: true only if they insist on exactly that many (else fewer results just make fewer charts). Use this — not widget.add + chart.setSymbol — whenever the charts' symbols come from a screen or watchlist. Never type tickers you have not been given.
manifest.shape: {"symbols":["NVDA"],"timeframe":"D","chart_type":null,"exact":null} or {"symbols":{"from":"<watchlist ref or screen as>","top":2},"timeframe":null,"chart_type":null,"exact":null}; timeframe 1|5|15|30|60|D|W|M (D daily, W weekly, M monthly, 60 hourly). No other keys: indicators, a row or a position cannot be set here — plan the charts alone and say in `reply` that indicators can be added next. ⛔ With NO chart in <workspace_context>, "add / open / show a <timeframe> chart of <symbol>" is THIS op on the workspace entry — never chart.setSymbol / chart.setTimeframe on a chart that does not exist.

manifest.name: layout.current
manifest.summary: Tell the member which named layout is open. UCT answers from the real state — use this (disposition apply) for "which layout am I on?" instead of answering yourself.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry.

manifest.name: layout.list
manifest.summary: List the member's named layouts. UCT answers from the real list — use this (disposition apply) whenever they ask what layouts they have, instead of listing them yourself.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry.

manifest.name: layout.open
manifest.summary: Open (switch to) one of the member's named layouts on the Charts workspace — exactly like clicking it in the Layout Dock.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; layout = the id of one entry in its `layouts` list, or the member's own words for it ("my trading layout" → "trading") — UCT matches the words itself: one match opens, several are asked about with the real names. Do not ask yourself. Only the open layout's widgets are in workspace_context; after a switch, ask again for changes on the new board.

manifest.name: layout.saveAs
manifest.summary: Save the current Charts workspace as a NEW named layout (it becomes the open layout). Never replaces an existing layout.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; name = the exact name the member gave. If that name is already in the layouts list, do not use this — tell the member instead. ONLY for saving the WORKSPACE/LAYOUT/BOARD: while an indicator draft is active (indicatorDrafts), "save it as X" means the indicator (indicator.saveDraft) unless the member says layout/workspace/board; if you cannot tell, ask.

manifest.name: layout.saveCurrent
manifest.summary: Save the board as it is now into the layout that is OPEN (only the member’s own layout). Replaces that layout’s saved copy; no Undo.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry. Use for "save these changes to my layout". For a NEW layout use layout.saveAs.

manifest.name: layout.rename
manifest.summary: Rename one of the member's OWN layouts (not prebuilt or built-in ones).
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; layout = the id of the layout to rename (the open one if they say "this layout"); name = the new name exactly as given. "rename <X> to <Y>" where X is a layout name = this op, never chart.renameTab (a chart widget's TAB, only when they say "tab"). A protected layout is refused by UCT itself: plan the op, never say you can't rename.

manifest.name: layout.create
manifest.summary: Create a NEW, EMPTY named layout (no widgets) for the member. The current board is not touched and the new layout is NOT opened.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; name = the exact name the member gave. To save the board AS IT IS NOW, use layout.saveAs instead. If they also want to switch to it, create it now and say in the reply that they can then say "open <name>" (switching is a separate step).

manifest.name: layout.delete
manifest.summary: Delete one of the member's OWN saved layouts (permanent). Not the layout that is open now, not prebuilt or built-in layouts.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; layout = the id of that layout in the layouts list. If more than one layout could be meant, or none matches exactly, clarify with the real names — never pick one by similarity. Deleting is always shown as a proposal first, so do not ask "are you sure?".

manifest.name: layout.duplicate
manifest.summary: Make a copy of a saved layout (its stored version) under a new name, as one of the member's own layouts. Does not open it.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; layout = the id of the layout to copy (the open one for "this layout"); name = the new name as given, or null when they give none (UCT names it "<name> copy" and the proposal shows it — do not ask for a name). To save the board AS IT IS NOW under a new name, use layout.saveAs instead.

manifest.name: watchlist.list
manifest.summary: List the member's saved watchlists (names and sizes). UCT answers from the real lists — use this (disposition apply) whenever they ask what watchlists they have.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the watchlistLibrary entry.

manifest.name: watchlist.show
manifest.summary: Say which symbols are in one of the member's watchlists. UCT answers from the real list — use this (disposition apply) for "what's in <list>?".
manifest.hints: target = the ref of that watchlist. "my watchlist" = the list a widget shows (shownInWidget); "the one I just made" = the list marked recent. as: name this list's STOCKS (e.g. "list1") when a later op in the same request uses them (e.g. widget.addCharts symbols {from:"list1", top:N}); else null.

manifest.name: watchlist.add
manifest.summary: Add tickers to one of the member's saved watchlists (the list itself, not a widget). Symbols already in the list are skipped.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist (or the "as" name of a list created earlier in this request); "my watchlist" = the list a widget shows (shownInWidget); "the one I just made" = the list marked recent. symbols = the tickers, uppercase, OR {from, top} to add a SCREEN's stocks: from = the "as" of a screener op earlier in this request (or "lastScreen" for the last screen run here), top = how many of its results, in its order (null = ALL of them — the default when they say "all" or give no number; at most 1000). Never type tickers you have not been given. If they say "my watchlist" and it is not clear which list, clarify with the real list names. One op per list.

manifest.name: watchlist.remove
manifest.summary: Remove specific tickers from one of the member's saved watchlists, one or several at once. Undo puts them back with their notes and order.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist; "my watchlist" = the list a widget shows (shownInWidget); "the one I just made" = the list marked recent. symbols = exactly the tickers to remove ("the top three" = the first rows of the listViews entry showing it, or of its symbols when no widget shows it). For "everything except these" use watchlist.keepOnly.

manifest.name: watchlist.keepOnly
manifest.summary: Remove everything from one of the member's saved watchlists EXCEPT the tickers named ("keep only these", "everything except these"). One change, always shown as a proposal naming what goes; Undo puts them back with their notes and order.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist; "my watchlist" = the list a widget shows (shownInWidget); "the one I just made" = the list marked recent. symbols = the tickers to KEEP ("keep the top three" = the first rows of the listViews entry showing it, or of its symbols). Every one must be in the list: a name that is not stops the whole change.

manifest.name: watchlist.clear
manifest.summary: Remove EVERY symbol from one of the member's saved watchlists (the list itself stays). Always shown as a proposal with the count first.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist. For only some symbols use watchlist.remove. If it is not clear which list, clarify with the real names.

manifest.name: watchlist.delete
manifest.summary: Delete one of the member's saved watchlists entirely (permanent). Not a list a Watchlist widget on this board is showing.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist. If more than one list could be meant, clarify with the real names — never pick one by similarity. Deleting is always shown as a proposal first, so do not ask "are you sure?". To empty a list but keep it, use watchlist.clear.

manifest.name: watchlist.create
manifest.summary: Create a NEW saved watchlist (a named list of tickers) — only when they ask to create or make a list. "Add a watchlist" with no list name means a Watchlist WIDGET on the board: that is widget.add, not this.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the watchlistLibrary entry; name = exactly as given. To COPY a list ("duplicate my X watchlist"), create "<X> copy" (or the name they give — do not ask for one) and add {from: the ref of X, top: null} to it. To fill it in the same request set "as" to a short name (new1) and target watchlist.add at that name; otherwise "as" is null. No name given: pick a short descriptive one (e.g. Software Over $10) not already in the watchlists list — do not ask. Never use this for a name already in the watchlists list — if they ask to put stocks in a list "called X" and X already exists, clarify (add to the existing X, or a new name); never silently append.

manifest.name: watchlist.rename
manifest.summary: Rename one of the member's saved watchlists.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist; name = the new name exactly as given.

manifest.name: watchlist.reorder
manifest.summary: Reorder one of the member's saved watchlists (the saved order, permanently): sort it alphabetically (A–Z or Z–A) and/or move some tickers to the top, in the order given. Nothing is added or removed. Undo puts the old order back.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist; sort = az | za | null (keep the order); top = tickers to put first, in this order ([] for none). "Sort my Momentum list" = az. This rewrites the saved order. To order what a widget shows by price, change or other data, use watchlist.sortColumn.

manifest.name: watchlist.setNote
manifest.summary: Write, change or clear the NOTE on one ticker in one of the member's saved watchlists (the note column on the Watchlists page). Undo puts the old note back.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist; symbol = the ticker (it must be in that list); note = the text exactly as the member gave it ("" clears it; at most 500 characters).

manifest.name: watchlist.sortColumn
manifest.summary: Sort what a Watchlist or Scanner widget shows by one of its columns (price, % change, RVOL, market cap…), the header click. It changes the view, not the saved order. column null = back to the saved order. Undo puts the old sort back.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the listViews entry: the one marked active for "this list", the one named as the list they name ("my Momentum list"; for "the one I just made", the watchlists entry marked recent), the only entry for "my watchlist"; several could be meant → clarify by name or position. No entry means no such widget is on this board: say so, offer watchlist.open. column = the column as they said it; direction = asc | desc | null (null = the header's own first click: Symbol A to Z, others high to low; "biggest / top / highest" = desc, "lowest / smallest" = asc). A column not showing is added. Columns: Price, Volume, % Change, Company Name, RVOL, IPO Date, Market Cap, Next Earnings, UCT Rating, $ Change, % from Open, % from High, % from Low, DCR, Dollar Volume, Sector, Industry, Theme, 5-Day, 30-Day, 60-Day, 90-Day, Attention, ATR %, ATR from 50SMA. For a permanent A to Z of the saved list use watchlist.reorder.

manifest.name: watchlist.setColumns
manifest.summary: Add or hide columns on a Watchlist or Scanner widget, or reset them to the defaults (the right-click column menu). Undo puts the old columns back.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the listViews entry: the one marked active for "this list", the one named as the list they name ("my Momentum list"; for "the one I just made", the watchlists entry marked recent), the only entry for "my watchlist"; several could be meant → clarify by name or position. No entry means no such widget is on this board: say so, offer watchlist.open. add / hide = columns as they said them ([] for none); reset = true only for "reset my columns" (the defaults, then add / hide). Symbol and the flag star can't be hidden. Columns: Price, Volume, % Change, Company Name, RVOL, IPO Date, Market Cap, Next Earnings, UCT Rating, $ Change, % from Open, % from High, % from Low, DCR, Dollar Volume, Sector, Industry, Theme, 5-Day, 30-Day, 60-Day, 90-Day, Attention, ATR %, ATR from 50SMA. Nothing else exists: a column not listed is refused, never swapped for a near one.

manifest.name: watchlist.step
manifest.summary: Move to the next or previous ticker in a Watchlist or Scanner widget, in the order it shows them (the arrow keys; the linked chart follows). Also first / last. Undo goes back to the ticker before.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the listViews entry: the one marked active for "this list", the one named as the list they name ("my Momentum list"; for "the one I just made", the watchlists entry marked recent), the only entry for "my watchlist"; several could be meant → clarify by name or position. No entry means no such widget is on this board: say so, offer watchlist.open. direction = next | previous | first | last; by = how many rows (null = 1): "next ticker" = next, "skip two" = next by 3. It wraps at the ends, as the arrow keys do. Never compute the ticker yourself.

manifest.name: watchlist.readView
manifest.summary: Say what a Watchlist or Scanner widget shows right now: its tickers in on-screen order (its column sort applied), its sort and columns. Use it for "what's at the top of this list". Its rows are in the listViews context too, so "remove the top three" can name them directly.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the listViews entry: the one marked active for "this list", the one named as the list they name ("my Momentum list"; for "the one I just made", the watchlists entry marked recent), the only entry for "my watchlist"; several could be meant → clarify by name or position. No entry means no such widget is on this board: say so, offer watchlist.open. as: name these STOCKS (e.g. "view1") when a later op in the same request uses them, e.g. watchlist.add symbols {from:"view1", top:3}; else null. It never reports prices.

manifest.name: watchlist.setFlag
manifest.summary: Flag or unflag tickers: the star on a row and Shift+F, one Flagged set across the whole app. Undo puts it back.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the flagged entry; symbols = the tickers, uppercase; flagged = true to flag, false to unflag. Never type tickers you have not been given: "this one" is the chart's symbol, "the top three" is the first rows of the listViews entry.

manifest.name: screener.run
manifest.summary: Run a stock screen on UCT's Screener and show the real matches (count + top rows). Changes nothing in UCT. Use this for "show me / find stocks with …".
manifest.hints: target = the screener entry ref. Comparisons, OR/NOT, rank: `compose`. filters: each {field: a key from `fields` (never invented), op, value, max, values}. Numbers: op gt|gte|lt|lte|eq|between, value, max (between only, else null), values null; % fields take 5 for 5%, $ fields take dollars (10M = 10000000). yes/no: op eq, value 1|0. (list) fields: op in|not_in, values = the member's own words (["software"]) — UCT matches real values; value/max null. "(latest session)" fields only when a session is named ("today", "yesterday"); "$10M a day" / "per day" if none named = the 30-day average, not share volume. A measure not in `fields`: say so, never substitute. sort_field/sort_dir or null. mode refine = change the LAST screen, else new. show: rows (null = 10, max 25). as: name the RESULT (screen1) when a later op uses its stocks ({from:"screen1", top:null} = all); else null. within: a watchlist ref only if they name that list ("in Momentum"); else null (whole market).
manifest.shape: a refinement that only changes the ORDER ("sort them by 3-month performance") is {"filters":[],"sort_field":"chg_pct_3m","sort_dir":"desc","mode":"refine","show":null,"as":null,"within":null,"logic":null,"rank":null} — filters is ALWAYS present ([] when nothing is added), sort_field is a key from `fields`, sort_dir is exactly "asc" or "desc" (never "descending"), and there is no nested "sort" object.

manifest.name: screener.runSaved
manifest.summary: Run one of the member's saved screens (or a UCT starter screen) and show the real matches.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry; screen = the id of an entry in savedScreens (never invent one; clarify with the real names if unsure). show: rows (null = 10). as: name its RESULT when a later op in the same request uses its stocks; else null.

manifest.name: screener.state
manifest.summary: Say what the last screen run here was: its filters, sort and number of matches.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry.

manifest.name: screener.listSaved
manifest.summary: List the member's saved screens and UCT's starter screens.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry.

manifest.name: alert.list
manifest.summary: Show the member's price alerts from UCT's real alert list: which are active, which went off (and when). Use this (disposition apply) for "show my alerts", "do I have an alert on NVDA?", "which alerts went off today?".
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the alertLibrary entry. symbol: one ticker to filter by, or null. status: active | triggered | all, or null (= all). triggered_today: true only for "today"; else null. These are PRICE alerts only — indicator alerts (RSI, MACD…) are not listed here.

manifest.name: alert.create
manifest.summary: Create ONE price alert in UCT's Alerts: it goes off ONCE when the stock is at or above (direction above) or at or below (direction below) a price level, checked while the market is open. Only price levels — no percent-move, indicator, volume or time alerts; alerts cannot be paused, edited or made repeating.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the alertLibrary entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase; price = the level as a number; direction = above ("crosses above", "breaks above", "rises to", "gets to … from below") or below ("drops below", "falls to", "breaks down under"). If they give a level WITHOUT saying above or below (e.g. "an alert on NVDA at 200", "when it hits 200"), clarify with choices above / below — never guess. One op per alert, at most 5 in one request. An earlier alert at that level that already went off does NOT stop a new one — create it. Creating is always shown to the member as a proposal first, so plan it (disposition propose) — even inside a question ("why is TSLA moving? and set an alert above 300": propose the alert AND ask research for the question). An alert on an indicator (RSI, MACD, a moving-average cross…) is indicatorAlert.create, not this. For a percent move, use disposition unsupported.

manifest.name: alert.delete
manifest.summary: Delete one of the member's price alerts (permanent — UCT cannot restore a deleted alert).
manifest.hints: target = the ref of that alert in the alerts list. One op per alert. Deleting is always shown to the member as a proposal first, so when the alert is clear (including "it" / "that one" right after an alert was named) plan the op — never ask "are you sure?". "All my inactive alerts" = one op per alert whose status is not active. If more than one alert could be the one they mean (e.g. two alerts on AMD), clarify with the real alerts as choices — never pick one. If the alerts list is not shown, use alert.list first.

manifest.name: indicatorAlert.list
manifest.summary: Show the member's indicator alerts from UCT's real list: symbol, indicator, condition, timeframe, whether each is active or paused, and why one can't fire. Use this (disposition apply) for "show my indicator alerts", "why hasn't my RSI alert fired".
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the indicatorAlertLibrary entry. symbol: one ticker, or null. status: active | paused | attention (alerts that can't fire) | null (all).

manifest.name: indicatorAlert.create
manifest.summary: Create ONE indicator alert on an indicator that is ON a chart (RSI above 70, MACD crossing a level, price touching a band, the 9 EMA crossing the 20 EMA, the member's own yes/no signal turning on), as the Indicator Alerts popover does. It watches that chart's symbol with the instance's own settings, on the chart's timeframe or another native one. Undo deletes it.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the indicatorAlertLibrary entry; instance = the id of the indicator from that chart's indicators entry (never a name); chart = the ref of the chart it is on; plot = null, or for several lines the address the catalog names (macd.signal) — not sure which line: ask. condition = above | below | cross_above | cross_below | cross_zero | touch_upper | touch_lower ("crosses above 70" = cross_above; "is over 70" = above); threshold = the level, else null. MA cross: instance = the 9, crossWith = the 20 (ids), cross_above|cross_below, threshold null; crossWith = null otherwise. The member's own yes/no signal: trigger = becomes_true ("turns on") | becomes_false ("turns off") | is_true, condition and threshold null; trigger = null otherwise. timeframe = null for the chart's own, or 1 | 5 | 15 | 30 | 60 | D | W | M ("alert on the weekly RSI" = W). A PRICE level ("when NVDA hits 150") is alert.create. Always proposed (disposition propose). Not on any chart: say to add it first.

manifest.name: indicatorAlert.toggle
manifest.summary: Pause or resume ONE indicator alert (the ON / OFF switch on its row in the chart's Indicator Alerts popover). Undo switches it back.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of that alert in the indicatorAlerts list; active = false to pause, true to resume. One op per alert.

manifest.name: indicatorAlert.delete
manifest.summary: Delete one of the member's indicator alerts (permanent — UCT cannot restore a deleted alert).
manifest.hints: target = the ref of that alert in the indicatorAlerts list. One op per alert. Always shown as a proposal first; if two alerts could be the one they mean, clarify with the real alerts as choices — never pick one. To stop one without deleting it, indicatorAlert.toggle.

manifest.name: stock.profile
manifest.summary: Answer a question about ONE stock's profile, price or fundamentals from UCT's own data: company name, sector/industry, price and today's change, market cap, P/E, 52-week range, revenue, margins, beta, next earnings date. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "what's NVDA's market cap?", "what sector is AMD in?", "what's TSLA's P/E?" instead of answering from memory.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase. Not for news or "why is it moving" (that needs research).

manifest.name: stock.earnings
manifest.summary: Answer earnings questions about ONE stock from UCT's earnings data: the latest REPORTED quarter's revenue and EPS versus consensus estimates, year-over-year change, and the next report date with its estimates. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "what was AMD's latest quarterly revenue?", "when does TSLA report earnings?", "did NVDA beat last quarter?".
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase.

manifest.name: stock.compare
manifest.summary: Compare the fundamentals of TWO stocks side by side from UCT's Research data (market cap, P/E, revenue, growth, margins, beta, next earnings). Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "compare NVDA and AMD".
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbols = exactly two tickers, uppercase. For three or more, clarify which two.

manifest.name: breadth.show
manifest.summary: MARKET BREADTH from UCT's own data (US, NYSE, Nasdaq): now, on a date or at the close (a close not finalized yet is labelled provisional), the last N sessions, two dates compared, or a range — % above a moving average, new highs/lows, advance/decline, Stage 2/4. UCT shows the figures; you never see them. Use this (disposition apply, research null), never state breadth figures yourself.
manifest.hints: target = breadth ref. universe us (default) | nyse | nasdaq | uct. metrics 1–4 keys; [] = general overview. value: date null = now; basis "close" if a close is asked; side "below" for % BELOW MA; else null. compare: compare_date. series: start, end null = latest. rows: sessions N = last N readings. Dates YYYY-MM-DD or null. reply: one short line, no figures. Keys: pct_above_{5,10,20,40,50,100,150,200}sma = % of stocks above that N-day simple MA; new_52w_highs/new_52w_lows = counts at 52-week highs/lows; net_new_high_low = highs minus lows; hi_ratio/lo_ratio = % of stocks at 52-week highs/lows; new_20d_highs/new_20d_lows = 20-day; near_52w_high = within 5% of 52w high; up_4pct_today/down_4pct_today = up/down 4%+ that day; ratio_5day/ratio_10day = up-4%/down-4% ratio over 5/10 days; adv_decline = net advancers; advancing/declining = issues up/down; universe_count = stocks counted; stage2_count/stage4_count = Stage 2 uptrend / Stage 4 downtrend counts.

manifest.name: breadth.history
manifest.summary: Search UCT's finalized daily MARKET BREADTH history (US, NYSE, Nasdaq) for when a condition held: the last/first time a measure was below/above a level, crossings, how many times, episodes and how long they lasted. UCT computes it and shows the member; you never see figures. Never say UCT lacks historical breadth.
manifest.hints: target = breadth entry ref. universe us (default) | nyse | nasdaq | uct; metric = ONE key (same keys as breadth.show). op below | at_or_below | above | at_or_above (strict unless at_or) | crosses_below | crosses_above; level in the measure's unit (10 = 10%). find last | first (date of the most recent / earliest match) | count (sessions + episodes; crossings for crosses_*) | episodes | longest | last_episode (runs of consecutive sessions). start / end YYYY-MM-DD or null (all history). aggregation "daily". A follow-up "that" / "it" = the measure and universe of the member's last breadth request. Lowest / highest in a period: breadth.show mode series. reply: one short line, no figures.

manifest.name: settings.show
manifest.summary: Say what the member's app settings are now (app theme, default chart timeframe, alert sound). Use this (disposition apply) for "show my settings".
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the settings entry.

manifest.name: settings.setAppTheme
manifest.summary: Change the WHOLE APP's colour theme (sidebar, panels, pages) — e.g. "switch to dark mode / light mode". Not a chart's colours: for one chart use chart.applyTheme.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the settings entry. theme: dark = Graphite (the default dark), oled = OLED Black, light = Light; or one of UCT's themes: slate (Slate, dark), graphite (Graphite, dark), carbon (Carbon, dark), navy (Midnight Navy, dark), forest (Deep Forest, dark), espresso (Espresso, dark), plum (Plum, dark), nord (Nord, dark), gunmetal (Gunmetal, dark), bordeaux (Bordeaux, dark), storm (Storm, dark), umber (Umber, dark), paper (Paper, light), cream (Cream, light), coolgray (Cool Gray, light), softblue (Soft Blue, light), sand (Sand, light), mint (Mint, light). "Dark mode" = dark; "light mode" = light.

manifest.name: settings.setDefaultTimeframe
manifest.summary: Change the timeframe NEW charts open on by default (Settings → Charts). Charts already on the board keep theirs — for one of those use chart.setTimeframe.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the settings entry. timeframe: 5 | 30 | 60 (minutes), D (daily), W (weekly) — the only choices Settings offers.

manifest.name: settings.setAlertSound
manifest.summary: Turn the in-app alert sound on or off, and/or pick which sound plays (Settings → Preferences → Alerts). Does not change whether alerts are delivered.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the settings entry. enabled: true | false | null (keep); sound: chime (Chime), bell (Bell), ding (Ding), double_tap (Double Tap), triple_pop (Triple Pop), radar (Radar), urgent (Urgent), soft (Soft), pulse (Pulse), major (Major Chord), or null (keep).

manifest.name: app.open
manifest.summary: Open another UCT page for the member, exactly like clicking it in the sidebar: the Screener, Dashboard, Breadth, Settings, a stock's Research page, etc. This closes this panel (the conversation is kept).
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the app entry. page: one of terminal (UCT Terminal), charts (Charts), morning-wire (Morning Wire), dashboard (Dashboard), ai-search (AI Search), uct-20 (UCT 20), breadth (Breadth), screener (Screener), options-flow (Options Flow), flow-scoreboard (Flow Record), live-massive (Live Flow), catalysts-history (Catalysts History), model-book (Model Book), formulas-reference (Formula Reference), desk (The Desk), journal (Journal), portfolio-heat (Portfolio Risk), community (Community), support (Support), settings (Settings), research (Research). section: only for page settings — account | billing | preferences | charts | compass | connections | legal — else null. symbol: only for page research (the ticker) — else null. Use this only when they ask to GO somewhere ("open / take me to / go to"); a question about data is answered here instead. Watchlists and Theme Tracker live on Charts (this page).

manifest.name: news.latest
manifest.summary: Show the latest news headlines UCT has stored for ONE stock (the Company Panel's News tab), each with time, source and tone. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "show me the latest NVDA news", "what news is UCT showing for PLTR".
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase; limit = how many headlines (null = 8, at most 15). For WHY a stock is moving right now, or a summary of today's news across the web, use research instead. To compare two stocks' news, one op per stock.

manifest.name: news.catalysts
manifest.summary: Show the catalysts UCT's catalyst engine has recorded for ONE stock (the Catalysts History page): the days it was flagged, catalyst type, grade, gap and the thesis written at the time. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "what are the recent catalysts for AMD?". UCT has no calendar of future events besides earnings (use stock.earnings for the next report).
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase.

manifest.name: settings.setWatchlistDigest
manifest.summary: Turn the member's watchlist EMAIL digest (a performance summary of their watchlists, emailed to their account email) on — daily or weekly — or off. Same as Settings → Email Digest.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the watchlistDigest entry; frequency = daily (every day 5 PM ET) | weekly (Fridays 5 PM ET) | off. Turning it on starts recurring emails: plan it (propose) and say so in the reply. To just see the current setting, answer from the watchlistDigest entry.

manifest.name: screener.saveAs
manifest.summary: Save the LAST screen run here (its exact filters, sort, ranking and logic) as a new saved screen in the member's Screener. Never replaces an existing one.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; name = the name as given. It saves the last screen run here — one run earlier in this conversation, or earlier in this same request. To run a NEW screen and save it in one request: the screen first, then this — it saves that screen.

manifest.name: screener.duplicateSaved
manifest.summary: Copy a saved screen (one of the member's or a UCT starter) to a new saved screen with exactly the same definition (filters, sort, ranking, logic, view, columns).
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of the screen to copy (from yours, or a starter id from the screener entry's savedScreens); name = the new name as given, or null for "<name> copy" (do not ask for a name).

manifest.name: screener.renameSaved
manifest.summary: Rename one of the member's own saved screens.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of one of YOUR screens; name = the new name as given.

manifest.name: screener.deleteSaved
manifest.summary: Delete one of the member's own saved screens (permanent). UCT's starter screens cannot be deleted.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of one of YOUR screens. If more than one could be meant, clarify with the real names — never pick one by similarity. Deleting is always shown as a proposal first, so do not ask "are you sure?".

manifest.name: widget.remove
manifest.summary: Remove a widget from the board (any type). Undo puts it back exactly — same place, size, link colour and settings. The space it leaves stays empty unless widget.arrange fills it.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the id of the widget from the board entry's widgets. If several could be meant, clarify — never guess.

manifest.name: widget.move
manifest.summary: Move and/or resize ONE widget to a rectangle on the board grid, exactly like dropping it there: the other widgets re-tile around it.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; x, y = the new top-left cell (columns from 0 at the left, rows from 0 at the top); w, h = the new width/height in cells, or null to keep the current size. The board entry gives the grid size and every widget's x/y/w/h. "to the left" = x 0; "narrower" = smaller w; "full height" = y 0 and h = rows.

manifest.name: widget.arrange
manifest.summary: Re-arrange widgets: "fill" grows them into the empty space around them (nothing else moves); "grid", "columns" or "rows" re-tile them evenly over the area they cover.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widgets = the ids to arrange, or null for every widget on the board; pattern = fill | grid | columns | rows. "make the remaining charts fill the space" = fill on those charts (after a widget.remove in the same plan).

manifest.name: chartGrid.set
manifest.summary: Show these tickers as that many charts, in equal cells: the charts already on the board are reused (top-left first), any still needed are ADDED, and the charts' area is re-tiled as an even grid. Other widgets stay; nothing is removed unless replace is set. One change, one Undo.
manifest.hints: Use for "create/open/show N charts for A, B, C…", "put SPY, QQQ, NVDA and TSLA in a 2x2 grid", "show NVDA and AMD side by side" — whenever the member names the tickers for several charts. target = the ref of the board entry. symbols = the tickers in the member's order, uppercase. timeframe = the one timeframe they gave for all of them (1|5|15|30|60 minutes, D, W, M), else null. layout = "columns" for side by side, "rows" for stacked, "grid" for a grid, else null. new_charts = true only when they ask for NEW charts ("in new charts", "add four new charts") — the charts already there then keep their tickers; else null. watchlist = true when they also ask for a watchlist beside the charts ("…, and a watchlist") and the board has none: a Watchlist widget is added in a cleared right column; else null. replace = true only when they chose to replace the board with this workspace, "charts" to replace only their charts, else null. Never widget.add + chart.setSymbol for this.

manifest.name: board.duplicateChart
manifest.summary: Duplicate one chart: its cell is split in two and a copy (same ticker, timeframe, look and indicators, not linked) appears in the other half. Nothing else moves. One change, one Undo.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id.

manifest.name: widget.setLink
manifest.summary: Set a widget's link colour: widgets with the same colour follow the same symbol; N = not linked.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; color = A (gold), B (blue), C (green), D (purple), E (red), F (teal), G (orange), H (pink), N (not linked) — E–H only when the board entry says extraLinkColors: true. "Link these two charts" = give both the same colour (use one already on one of them).

manifest.name: widget.showList
manifest.summary: Make a Watchlist widget show one of the member's own watchlists (what picking it in the widget does).
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the id of a watchlist widget; list = the ref of the watchlist (from watchlists).

manifest.name: widget.setOption
manifest.summary: Change ONE option of a widget on the board — what its own settings control writes (a Fundamentals view, a News filter, an Options Flow lead / scope, the Calendar's star filter, Volume Scan logos…). Undo puts the previous value back.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the widget id; key = the option name from the widget type's own list below (never invented); value = one of its allowed values. Options by widget type — fundamentals: view (annual|quarterly|analyst|ownership); news: filter (all|up|down); calendar: econStars (1–3); optionsflow: lead (tape|biggest|sentiment), scope (market|symbol); periodsort: group (theme|sector|industry); volumescan: showLogos (on/off); tradeExchangeNews: follow (on/off), linked (on/off); researchLibrary: follow (on/off), linked (on/off). A widget type not listed has no options here.

manifest.name: watchlist.open
manifest.summary: Open one of the member's watchlists in their workspace: the Watchlist widget on this board shows it (with none, a Watchlist widget is added in empty space). Use for "open it / show it in my workspace".
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; list = the ref of the watchlist, or the "as" name of a list created earlier in this request (it opens after that list is created and filled).

manifest.name: widget.showScan
manifest.summary: Make a Scanner widget show one of UCT's scans (what picking it in the widget does).
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the id of a scanner widget; scan = highest-volume-1y (Highest Volume In 1-Year), highest-volume-ever (Highest Volume Ever), ipo-1y (IPO in Last 1-Year), top-gainers-30d (Top Gainers (30-Day)), top-gainers-60d (Top Gainers (60-Day)), top-gainers-90d (Top Gainers (90-Day)).

manifest.name: chart.applyThemeAll
manifest.summary: Apply one of UCT's chart themes to EVERY chart on the board (and chart tabs), exactly as the theme gallery's "all charts" does; new charts on this layout start with it.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; theme = a chart theme id (the same ids as chart.applyTheme). For ONE chart use chart.applyTheme.

manifest.name: widget.resize
manifest.summary: Resize ONE widget by moving one of its edges, exactly like dragging that edge: the widget the edge moves into shrinks (never below its minimum); nothing leaves the board.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; edge = left | right | top | bottom; by = cells to move the edge OUTWARD (positive = bigger, negative = smaller). "Make my watchlist narrower and give the chart more space" = resize the CHART toward the watchlist (the watchlist shrinks), or the watchlist inward then widget.arrange fill on the chart.

manifest.name: board.swap
manifest.summary: Swap two widgets' places on the board. Side by side (same rows) or stacked (same columns): each keeps its own size and they trade sides. Otherwise only two widgets of the same size can trade cells. Nothing else moves.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; a, b = the two widgets' ids. "move my watchlist to the right" when the chart is on the right = swap the watchlist and that chart.

manifest.name: widget.selectTab
manifest.summary: Switch a widget to one of its tabs (clicking the tab in the widget header).
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; tab = "main" (the widget's own content), "1", "2"… or the tab's name, from the board entry's widgetTabs. NOT chart tabs (those are chart.*Tab).

manifest.name: widget.renameTab
manifest.summary: Rename one of a widget's tabs (double-click the tab), or clear the name back to the automatic label. At most 24 characters.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; tab = "main" (the widget's own content), "1", "2"… or the tab's name, from the board entry's widgetTabs. NOT chart tabs (those are chart.*Tab). name = the new name, or null to go back to the automatic label.

manifest.name: widget.closeTab
manifest.summary: Close one of a widget's extra tabs (its ×); the widget's own main tab cannot be closed. Undo puts the tab back exactly, settings included.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; tab = "main" (the widget's own content), "1", "2"… or the tab's name, from the board entry's widgetTabs. NOT chart tabs (those are chart.*Tab).

manifest.name: widget.addTab
manifest.summary: Add another widget as a TAB inside an existing (non-chart) widget — the widget header's "+" — and show it. Nothing else on the board moves. Undo closes it.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; type = one of chart, watchlist, themes, scanner, fundamentals, breadth, aisearch, news, notebook, profile, alerts, calendar, optionsflow, nhnl, nhnlPulse, volumescan, scatter. For a chart's own tabs (symbols, timeframes) use chart.addTab.

manifest.name: chart.addTab
manifest.summary: Add a new chart TAB to a chart widget (the tab strip's "+"), on the same link colour as the tab showing now, and switch to it.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; timeframe = 1|5|15|30|60|D|W|M or null (daily); name = a label for the tab or null. The new tab follows the same symbol until its link colour is changed (chart.linkTab). Only when the member asks for a TAB: several CHARTS ("on four charts", "N charts for …") are chartGrid.set or widget.addCharts, never tabs of one chart.

manifest.name: chart.selectTab
manifest.summary: Switch a chart widget to one of its tabs (clicking the tab).
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; tab = "main" (the widget's own chart), the extra tab's position "1", "2"… or its label, from the board entry's chartTabs.

manifest.name: chart.closeTab
manifest.summary: Close one EXTRA tab of a chart widget (its settings go with it; Undo brings it back exactly). The main tab cannot be closed.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; tab = "main" (the widget's own chart), the extra tab's position "1", "2"… or its label, from the board entry's chartTabs.

manifest.name: chart.renameTab
manifest.summary: Rename a chart widget's tab (double-click on the tab).
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; tab = "main" (the widget's own chart), the extra tab's position "1", "2"… or its label, from the board entry's chartTabs. name = the new label (24 characters at most).
manifest.shape: only for a chart widget's TAB the member names as a tab ("rename the tab"). "rename <a layout name> to …" is layout.rename.

manifest.name: chart.linkTab
manifest.summary: Set the link colour of one chart TAB (the tab's colour dot): tabs and widgets with the same colour follow the same symbol.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; tab = "main" (the widget's own chart), the extra tab's position "1", "2"… or its label, from the board entry's chartTabs. color = A (gold), B (blue), C (green), D (purple), E (red), F (teal), G (orange), H (pink) (E–H only when the board entry says extraLinkColors: true) — a tab is always linked to a colour. "Two tabs with linked symbols" = give both the same colour.

manifest.name: drawing.addTrendline
manifest.summary: Draw a TRENDLINE between two points (date + price each) on a chart's symbol — the toolbar's own trendline tool. Every chart on that symbol shows it; Undo removes it.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; from / to = {date, price}: the two anchors in time order ("from the Oct 15 low at 180 to last Friday at 195"). A point the member describes without a date AND a price ("the recent low") has no anchor — clarify, never guess. a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented; color = a colour name or #hex, null = the member's drawing default; style = solid | dashed | dotted, null = solid.

manifest.name: drawing.addRay
manifest.summary: Draw a RAY from one point (date + price) through a second, extended to the right — the toolbar's own ray tool. Every chart on that symbol shows it; Undo removes it.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; from = the start {date, price}; to = a second point it passes through {date, price}, after the first. a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented; color = a colour name or #hex, null = the member's drawing default; style = solid | dashed | dotted, null = solid.

manifest.name: drawing.addRectangle
manifest.summary: Draw a RECTANGLE between two opposite corners (date + price each) on a chart's symbol — the toolbar's own rectangle. Undo removes it.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; from / to = {date, price}: opposite corners ("a box from Oct 1 at 170 to Oct 20 at 185"). a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented; color = a colour name or #hex, null = the member's drawing default; style = solid | dashed | dotted, null = solid.

manifest.name: drawing.addFib
manifest.summary: Draw a FIBONACCI RETRACEMENT between two points (date + price each) on a chart's symbol — the toolbar's own tool with its standard levels. Undo removes it.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; from = the swing start {date, price} (the low for an up move); to = the swing end {date, price}. "Fib from the Oct 7 low at 150 to the Oct 28 high at 190". a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented; color = a colour name or #hex, null = the member's drawing default; style = solid | dashed | dotted, null = solid.

manifest.name: drawing.addHorizontalRay
manifest.summary: Draw a HORIZONTAL RAY from a date at a price, extending to the right — the toolbar's own horizontal ray (a level that starts on a day, e.g. a breakout level from its breakout date). Undo removes it.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; date = where the ray starts; price = its level; a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented; color / style as for other drawings (null = defaults). A level with no start date is drawing.addLevel.

manifest.name: drawing.addText
manifest.summary: Place a TEXT NOTE on a chart's symbol at a date and price — the toolbar's own text tool, with the member's exact words. Undo removes it.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; text = the note exactly as the member said it (never reworded, up to 200 characters); date / price = where it sits; a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented; color = a colour name or #hex, null = the member's default.

manifest.name: drawing.addAvwap
manifest.summary: Draw an ANCHORED VWAP on a chart's symbol starting from a date — the toolbar's own anchored VWAP (volume-weighted average price from that session forward). Undo removes it.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; date = the anchor session (a trading day: an earnings day, a low, "last friday"); price = the price on that day the member named, or the price they are looking at there (the anchor's level — the VWAP itself is computed from the bars); a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented; color null = the member's default.

manifest.name: drawing.list
manifest.summary: List the drawings on a chart's symbol (every chart on that symbol shares them): each one's id, tool, level and style. Read-only.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol.

manifest.name: drawing.addLevel
manifest.summary: Draw a HORIZONTAL LINE at a price on a chart's symbol — the price axis's own "Draw horizontal line at $X". Every chart on that symbol shows it; Undo removes it. A level that starts on a date is drawing.addHorizontalRay; every other tool has its own capability or drawing.add.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; price = the level (a number, as the member said it — never invented); color = a colour name or #hex, null = the member's drawing default; style = solid | dashed | dotted, null = solid. One op per level. A level the member describes without a number ("the recent high", "support") has no price — clarify, never guess.

manifest.name: drawing.style
manifest.summary: Change ONE drawing's colour, line style or width (what its settings do). Undo puts the old style back.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id from that entry's drawings (the most recent one the member drew is last; the one marked recent is the one I last drew or changed); color / style / width null = leave as is. "Make that line pink and dashed" / "make it red" = the recent one (else the line just drawn).

manifest.name: drawing.remove
manifest.summary: Remove ONE drawing by id from a chart's symbol (every chart and layout showing it). Refused for a locked drawing and for one an alert is attached to. A hidden drawing is shown as a proposal first. Undo puts it back.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id. "Remove the line I just added" = the newest one (or the one marked recent). To remove EVERY drawing use drawing.clear.

manifest.name: drawing.setVisible
manifest.summary: Show or hide ONE drawing (its eye in the drawing's menu) on a chart's symbol — every chart on that symbol. Nothing is deleted. Undo puts it back.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id; visible = true to show, false to hide. For EVERY drawing on the symbol use drawing.setAllVisible.

manifest.name: drawing.lock
manifest.summary: Lock or unlock ONE drawing (its lock in the drawing's menu): a locked drawing can't be moved, restyled or removed until it is unlocked. Undo puts it back.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id; locked = true to lock, false to unlock.

manifest.name: drawing.setLevel
manifest.summary: Move a HORIZONTAL line (or a horizontal ray) to a new price — what dragging it does. Refused for a locked drawing. A line an alert is attached to is shown first (its alert moves with it). Undo puts it back.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = the horizontal line's id (the one marked recent for "move it"); price = the new level as the member said it — never invented.

manifest.name: drawing.setAllVisible
manifest.summary: Show or hide EVERY drawing on a chart's symbol at once (every chart on that symbol). Nothing is deleted. Undo puts each one back as it was.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry; visible = true to show them all, false to hide them all.

manifest.name: drawing.clear
manifest.summary: Remove EVERY drawing on a chart's symbol (every chart and layout showing it) — always shown as a proposal first. Locked drawings and drawings with an alert attached are kept (and said). Undo puts them all back.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol.

manifest.name: drawing.add
manifest.summary: Draw any other toolbar tool from dates and prices: extended line, vertical line, circle, arrow, Fibonacci extension, pitchfork, parallel channel, cup curve, Measure, Price Range, Bars & Time or Price Move. Every chart on that symbol shows it; Undo removes it.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry for the chart's symbol; points = [{date, price}, …] in the tool's order: extended: first point, second point; vertical: the date (price null); circle: one corner, opposite corner; arrow: tail, tip; fibext: move start, move end; pitchfork: pivot, left shoulder, right shoulder; channel: base start, base end, a point on the parallel line; cup: left rim, bottom, right rim; measure: start, end; priceRange: start, end; dateRange: start, end; advance: setup candle, candle where the move tops. a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented; a point with no number ("the low") has no anchor — clarify, never guess. color / style null = defaults.

manifest.name: drawing.setAnchors
manifest.summary: Move the anchors of ONE drawing (what dragging its points does): any tool, any point, a new date and/or price. "Flatten that line" sets every point to the first point's price. Refused for a locked drawing. A drawing with an alert is shown first (its alert follows). Undo puts it back.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id (the recent one for "it"); points = [{point, date, price}]: point 1 = the first of that drawing's `anchors`, date / price null = keep it. "Move the second point to Nov 1 at 210" = one item; a whole drawing up $5 = one item per point, from its anchors. a date is YYYY-MM-DD or the member's words (today, yesterday, last friday, oct 15, 10/15); price = the number the member said — never invented.

manifest.name: drawing.setProps
manifest.summary: Change settings on ONE drawing, as its right-click menu does: fill, price label, percent label, arrow size, Measure label fields and position, a note's words, font, size, bold, italic, background, border. Each tool has only its own settings; one it lacks is refused and its real ones named. Colour, width and line style are drawing.style. Undo puts them back.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id; set = [{prop, value, opacity}]. prop by tool: rectangle fillColor, showPercentChange; horizontal line / ray showPriceLabel; arrow arrowSize (small | medium | large); Measure / Price Range showDollar, showPercent, showBars, showTime, labelPos (top | center | bottom); Bars & Time showBars, showTime, labelPos; Price Move showDollar, showPercent; note text, fontFamily, fontSize (8-64), bold, italic, bgEnabled, bgColor, borderEnabled, borderColor. value = true / false for a switch, a colour, null = back to default. opacity = 0-100 for a colour, null = default.

manifest.name: drawing.setFibLevels
manifest.summary: Edit a Fibonacci retracement or extension's Levels… menu: show or hide a level, colour a level, turn the fill between two neighbouring levels on or off and colour it, or reset them all to defaults. The anchors and any level alerts are not touched. Undo puts them back.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = the Fibonacci's id. levels = [{level, visible, color}], level as the member says it (0.786 or 78.6), visible false = "remove the 78.6"; null = leave. bands = [{from, to, enabled, color, opacity}] between two neighbouring levels, color null = its default, opacity = 0-100 or null. reset = true for "reset the fib levels" (levels and bands then both []). Levels are the tool's own table: there are no custom levels.

manifest.name: drawing.setAlert
manifest.summary: Set an alert that FOLLOWS a drawing (the drawing menu's "Set alert…"): a trendline, ray, extended line, horizontal line or ray, or one Fibonacci level. A sloped line's level moves with time; moving the drawing moves the alert. Always shown first; Undo removes the alert unless it already went off.
manifest.hints: target = the drawings entry; drawing = its id; direction = above ("breaks above", "gets above") or below ("breaks below", "loses"). If they do not say which side, clarify — never guess. level = the Fibonacci level (0.618 or 61.8), else null. Plan it, disposition propose. For a price with no drawing use alert.create.

manifest.name: indicator.list
manifest.summary: List the indicators on ONE chart (as its legend names them): built-in or custom, shown or hidden, on the price chart or in its own pane. UCT answers from the chart's real state — use this (disposition apply) whenever they ask what indicators are on a chart, whether one is on, or which are hidden, instead of answering yourself.
manifest.hints: target = the indicators entry for the chart the member means (with several charts and no chart named, ask which). filter: hidden | shown | null (all).

manifest.name: indicator.openCreate
manifest.summary: Open the Create Indicator PANEL (the visual builder) on one chart — ONLY when the member asks for the panel by name ("open Create Indicator"), or to Modify a saved custom indicator there. Their request is typed into its box; nothing is built or saved. To BUILD an indicator with the member in this chat, use indicator.draft.
manifest.hints: target = the indicators entry for the chart. request = the member's description of the indicator, in their words (≤ 600 characters), or null to just open it. defId = a custom indicator's defId from that chart's list (only to modify it), else null — never a name. Use ONLY for an explicit request to open the panel ("open Create Indicator", "open the indicator builder/editor") or to modify a saved custom indicator there. "Build/make/create/write me an indicator…" is indicator.draft (built right here in the chat), not this. Adding, removing, showing or hiding indicators on a chart is indicator.add/remove/show/hide.

manifest.name: indicator.add
manifest.summary: Add ONE indicator to ONE chart — exactly what the Indicator Library's Add to Chart does. Built-in indicators or the member's own saved ones; Undo removes it again.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. defId = an id from indicatorCatalog (never invented, never a name). The SAME indicator on several charts = one indicator.add per chart named, same defId; if it isn't clear which charts, ask. Classic overlay averages (the legacy EMA/SMA rows) and Volume Profile are NOT added this way — say they live in Chart Settings. inputs = null for the indicator's defaults, else [{key, value}] with ONLY keys from that row's `settings` ("a 20 EMA" → movingAverage, [{key:"period",value:20},{key:"maType",value:"ema"}]; "RSI 7" → rsi, [{key:"period",value:7}]). Every number or type the member named goes in inputs — never drop one or add a default instead. A setting the row does not list: say it isn't available; never guess a key. A moving average named by its LENGTH only ("the 9 and 20", "a 50 ma"): EMA for 8, 9, 10, 20 and 21, SMA for 50 and above (the member's default — say which you used); any other length: ask EMA or SMA.

manifest.name: indicator.remove
manifest.summary: Remove ONE indicator (its whole group, e.g. all COT panes) from ONE chart — the settings ✕ / legend Delete. Always shown as a proposal first, listing anything it would disconnect. Undo restores it exactly (same identity, reconnected inputs).
manifest.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

manifest.name: indicator.update
manifest.summary: Change the settings of ONE indicator already on ONE chart, in place — its length, its moving-average type, or another setting its row lists (what the indicator's settings dialog does). Never adds a second copy. Undo puts the old settings back.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). inputs = [{key, value}] with ONLY keys from that indicator's settings, and ONLY the settings the member named — everything else stays as it is (an EMA stays an EMA unless they name a type). "make it a 9" right after adding an EMA 20 → that EMA, [{key:"period",value:9}]; "change that to an SMA" → [{key:"maType",value:"sma"}]. Use this — never indicator.remove + indicator.add — to change an indicator that is already on the chart.

manifest.name: indicator.show
manifest.summary: Show ONE indicator (its whole group) on ONE chart — the settings / legend eye. Undo puts it back.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

manifest.name: indicator.hide
manifest.summary: Hide ONE indicator (its whole group) on ONE chart — the settings / legend eye. Undo puts it back.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

manifest.name: indicator.draft
manifest.summary: THE DEFAULT for building a custom indicator: build it WITH the member right here in this chat ("build/make me an indicator that…", "also require RSI above 50", "what would you add?") — one draft, through Create Indicator's own engine. Questions and advice change nothing. Never saves (indicator.saveDraft does).
manifest.hints: target = the ACTIVE draft's ref to continue it (follow-ups like "also…", "make it…", "what would you add?" go to the active draft); the NEW-draft entry only when the member starts a different indicator or edits one of yourIndicators (edit = its defId, else null). With an active draft, "this indicator" / "the indicator" / "it" means that draft — do not ask which. If several drafts could be meant and none is active or named, ask which. chart = the ref of the chart the member names for it, else null (a draft keeps its own chart). message = the member's words, verbatim — never your own formula or interpretation. NEVER add indicator.previewDraft unless the member asked in this message to see/preview it.

manifest.name: indicator.previewDraft
manifest.summary: Show an indicator draft as this tab's ONE live preview on a chart (not saved; moves off any other chart). Only when the member asks to see it.
manifest.hints: target = the draft's ref (usually the active one). chart = the ref of the chart to preview on — the one the member names, or the only chart; if several charts and none named, ask which. Never preview unasked.

manifest.name: indicator.saveDraft
manifest.summary: Save an indicator draft as one of the member's indicators (Create Indicator's own Save; a new indicator, or a new version of the one being edited) — always shown as a proposal with the builder's own summary first. addTo: charts to add the SAVED indicator to afterwards (each added separately, with its own receipt).
manifest.hints: Use when the member saves THE INDICATOR: "save it", "save it as X", "save the indicator/draft" while an indicator draft is active (the active indicatorDrafts entry) — that "it" is the draft, NOT the workspace layout (layout.saveAs is only for an explicit layout/workspace/board). target = the draft's ref (usually the active one). name = the name the member gave ("save it as Bullish Trend" → "Bullish Trend"), else null — never a separate indicator.draft op for the name. addTo = [] UNLESS the member asked in this message to add/apply/put it on a chart; then only the charts' refs from the charts section that they named. Saving and adding to a chart are separate intents. "Save the indicator" with one active draft is that draft — do not ask which.

manifest.name: indicator.undoDraft
manifest.summary: Undo the last change in an indicator draft, exactly, when there is nothing of mine to Undo (e.g. after a reload). Never touches a chart or a saved indicator.
manifest.hints: target = the draft's ref. Only for "undo the last change to my draft" when the normal Undo has nothing.

manifest.name: indicator.discardDraft
manifest.summary: Throw away ONE unsaved indicator draft ("never mind that indicator", "discard the draft"). Always shown as a proposal first. Saved indicators and charts are never touched.
manifest.hints: target = the draft's ref (usually the active one). Only a draft — to remove an indicator from a chart use indicator.remove.

manifest.name: chartSetup.copyLook
manifest.summary: Make ONE chart look like another chart on the board: it takes the other chart's colours, theme, chart type, scale and display settings. Its own indicators, comparisons and timeframe menu stay exactly as they are. Shown as a proposal first; Undo puts the old look back.
manifest.hints: target = the chart that CHANGES; from = the ref of the chart to copy the look FROM. "Make the left chart look like the right one" → target = left, from = right.

manifest.name: chartSetup.removeTimeframe
manifest.summary: Remove a CUSTOM timeframe (e.g. 45 minutes, 2 hours) from ONE chart's timeframe menu — the menu's own ✕. Built-in timeframes cannot be removed. Undo puts it back.
manifest.hints: timeframe = the custom code as the chart lists it (e.g. "45", "2h", "3D") or words ("45m", "2 hours").

manifest.name: chartSetup.favoriteTimeframe
manifest.summary: Star or un-star a timeframe on ONE chart (the timeframe menu's ★): starred timeframes show in the chart's header bar. Undo puts it back.
manifest.hints: timeframe = a code (1, 5, 15, 30, 60, D, W, M, or a custom one the chart has); favorite = true to star, false to un-star.

manifest.name: chartSetup.compareDisplay
manifest.summary: Change how ONE chart's comparison overlays are shown (Tools → Compare Symbols): each overlay's scale ("same" = share the main price scale, "new" = its own % scale), showing or hiding an overlay, and "Group only" (hide the chart's own symbol). To add or remove overlays use chart.compare.
manifest.hints: symbols = the compared tickers this applies to ([] = every comparison on the chart); scale = same | new | null (keep); visible = true | false | null (keep); groupOnly = true | false | null (keep).

manifest.name: chartSetup.setRange
manifest.summary: Show ONE chart over a set date range: the range bar's buttons (3M, 6M, YTD, 1Y, 5Y, Origin; Origin = from the first bar). A view change: every bar stays on the chart, nothing is drawn or removed, and the chart keeps this window on the next ticker until it is panned or reset. Undo puts the previous view back.
manifest.hints: range = one of 3M, 6M, YTD, 1Y, 5Y, Origin. "One year" = 1Y, "year to date" = YTD, "five years" = 5Y, "since IPO" = Origin. Other spans have no button: use chart.goToDate, or say which ranges exist.

manifest.name: chartSetup.resetView
manifest.summary: Reset ONE chart's view (right-click → Reset view): the default window with the newest bar in place, and the price scale back on auto. A view change: settings, drawings and indicators are untouched. No Undo.
manifest.hints: target = the chart. For a chart's SETTINGS use chart.resetDefaults.

manifest.name: chartSetup.setIndicatorsHidden
manifest.summary: Hide or bring back EVERYTHING drawn over the candles on ONE chart at once (Alt+Shift+I): every indicator, every moving average and Volume. Temporary: a reload brings them back, nothing is removed or saved. To hide just the moving averages use chartSetup.setMovingAverages; for one indicator, indicator.hide.
manifest.hints: hidden = true to hide them all, false to bring them back.

manifest.name: chartSetup.setMovingAverages
manifest.summary: Hide or show EVERY moving average on ONE chart at once (Ctrl+M). They stay on the chart, hidden, and this is saved. Other indicators are untouched. Undo puts each one back as it was.
manifest.hints: visible = false to hide them all, true to show them all.

manifest.name: chartSetup.saveTemplate
manifest.summary: Save ONE chart's current settings as one of the member's chart templates (Chart Settings → Templates → Save as Template) — its look and its indicators, exactly what the button saves. A template with the same name is replaced (then it is shown first). Undo puts the old list back.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the chartTemplateLibrary entry; chart = the ref of the chart to save from; name = exactly as the member said it (at most 40 characters).

manifest.name: chartSetup.deleteTemplate
manifest.summary: Delete one of the member's saved chart templates (a template's ✕ in Chart Settings → Templates). Charts that used it keep their settings. Shown first; Undo puts it back.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the chartTemplateLibrary entry; name = a template name from that entry, exactly.

manifest.name: indicatorStyle.set
manifest.summary: Change how ONE indicator on ONE chart looks — its colour (or a histogram's up / down colours), line width, line style, plot style, or which chart timeframes it shows on — exactly what its settings / Inspector offer. One change per op; Undo puts it back.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry; instance = the indicator's id from that chart's indicators list (or "#20" for the one of length 20, "#20:ema"). property = color | upColor | downColor | lineWidth (1–4, or "thicker" / "thinner") | lineStyle (solid | dashed | dotted) | plotStyle (line, histogram, area… as offered) | overlap | showOn (which chart timeframes it draws on: value = "daily", "weekly", "daily and weekly", "intraday", "daily and above" or "all" — "only show it on the daily" = showOn daily). value = the member's value (a colour name or #hex for colours). output = which line or colour when the indicator has several (its label), else null. "Make the 9 green and the 20 red and dashed" = three ops.

manifest.name: indicatorStyle.placeIn
manifest.summary: Move ONE indicator on ONE chart to where it draws — on the price pane, on the volume pane, in its own pane, inside another indicator's pane, or back to automatic (the Inspector's "Display in"). Undo puts it back.
manifest.hints: target = the chart's indicatorEdits entry; instance = the indicator; place = price | volume | pane (its own) | auto | another indicator on that chart (its id or name) to draw inside its pane.

manifest.name: pane.move
manifest.summary: Reorder ONE chart's panes (Chart Data → Arrange): move a pane up, down, to the top or bottom, or above / below another pane ("move RSI above price"). Undo puts the order back.
manifest.hints: target = the chart's indicatorEdits entry; pane = price | volume | an indicator drawn in its own pane (its id, name or kind, e.g. "rsi"); to = up | down | top | bottom | above | below; relativeTo = the other pane for above / below, else null.

manifest.name: pane.resize
manifest.summary: Change the height of ONE pane on ONE chart (what dragging its divider does): a percent of the chart's height, bigger, smaller, or back to automatic. Undo puts it back.
manifest.hints: target = the chart's indicatorEdits entry; pane = price | volume | an indicator in its own pane; size = a percent (4–90) or "bigger" | "smaller" | "auto".

manifest.name: indicatorCopy.duplicate
manifest.summary: Add a second copy of ONE indicator on the same chart, with everything it is configured with (the legend's Duplicate). Undo removes only the copy.
manifest.hints: target = the chart's indicatorEdits entry; instance = the indicator to copy. To put indicators on ANOTHER chart use indicatorCopy.copyTo.

manifest.name: indicatorCopy.copyTo
