manifest.summary: Copy indicators from one chart onto ANOTHER chart, exactly as configured (colours, settings, panes and links between them — the Indicator templates copy). One op per destination chart; an indicator already there is skipped and said. Undo removes what was added.
manifest.hints: target = the DESTINATION chart's indicatorEdits entry; from = the ref of the chart to copy FROM; instances = the indicators to copy (ids or names from that chart), or [] for all of them. "Copy these indicators to all my charts" = one op per other chart.

manifest.name: indicatorTemplate.list
manifest.summary: List the member's saved INDICATOR templates and the indicators in each, from the real list. Use this (disposition apply) for "what indicator templates do I have".
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the indicatorTemplateLibrary entry.

manifest.name: indicatorTemplate.apply
manifest.summary: Add the indicators of ONE saved INDICATOR template to ONE chart, each exactly as saved. Nothing on the chart is removed; one already there is skipped and said. Undo removes what was added. A CHART template (look and settings) is chart.applyTemplate instead.
manifest.hints: target = the chart's indicatorEdits entry. template = a name from indicatorTemplateLibrary, exactly. Several charts = one op per chart; if it isn't clear which charts, ask. A name in both that entry and chartTemplates: ask which they mean.

manifest.name: indicatorTemplate.save
manifest.summary: Save the indicators on ONE chart as a named INDICATOR template (settings, colours, panes; no alerts). A template with that name is replaced only after the member approves it. Undo puts the list back. A chart's whole look is chartSetup.saveTemplate instead.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the indicatorTemplateLibrary entry; chart = the ref of the chart to save from; name = exactly as the member said it (at most 40 characters). It saves every indicator on that chart.

manifest.name: indicatorTemplate.delete
manifest.summary: Delete one of the member's saved INDICATOR templates. Indicators already on charts stay. Shown first; Undo puts it back. A chart template is chartSetup.deleteTemplate instead.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the indicatorTemplateLibrary entry; name = a name from that entry, exactly.

manifest.name: definition.search
manifest.summary: Find indicators by name or what they do — UCT's built-in indicators and the member's own saved ones (never anyone else's). Read-only.
manifest.hints: target = the definitionLibrary entry; query = the member's words ("momentum", "volatility bands", "my trend"); kind = builtin | custom | null (both).

manifest.name: definition.describe
manifest.summary: Describe ONE indicator — its settings and their ranges, what it outputs, where it draws, and whether each output can drive an alert or a scan. Read-only.
manifest.hints: target = the definitionLibrary entry; defId = its id (from a search or a chart's indicators list), or its exact name.

manifest.name: definition.duplicate
manifest.summary: Save a COPY of an indicator as one of the member's own indicators (the legend's "Create custom copy") — a built-in becomes an editable formula, one of theirs is forked. Shown first; Undo deletes the copy (while no chart draws it).
manifest.hints: target = the definitionLibrary entry; defId = the indicator's id (or its exact name). To put an indicator on a chart twice use indicatorCopy.duplicate instead.

manifest.name: definition.delete
manifest.summary: Delete one of the member's OWN saved indicators (built-ins cannot be deleted). Always shown first, naming every chart still drawing it (they stop drawing it). Undo restores it under the same id, so those charts draw it again.
manifest.hints: target = the definitionLibrary entry; defId = the indicator's id from yourIndicators or a chart's indicators list (or its exact name). If more than one of theirs could be meant, ask — never pick by similarity.

manifest.name: agent.capabilities
manifest.summary: Answer what UCT Agent can and cannot do (now, partly, not yet, planned) about a topic — from UCT's own capability list, never from memory.
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the agent entry. Use ONLY for a question ABOUT abilities ("can you draw trendlines?", "what can you do with layouts?", "can you backtest?"). A polite request to DO something you can do ("can you switch this to weekly?") is a command: plan it, do not use this. topic: overview for "what can you do?"; other when no topic fits.

manifest.name: agent.undo
manifest.summary: Undo YOUR OWN most recent change(s) in this conversation — exactly what the Undo on that change’s receipt does. UCT refuses it itself when that change can’t be undone (changed since, another board, a protected layout, a permanent action).
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the agent entry. scope: "last" = the newest change (undo that / undo the last change / revert it); "all" = every change of the previous request (undo all of that). about = what the member says the change was ("undo the timeframe change" → timeframe), else null. In a request that makes a change AND undoes it ("switch to weekly, then undo that"), put the change first and agent.undo LAST. Never tell the member you cannot undo, or to use another Undo: plan this, and UCT reports what it actually undid.

manifest.name: guide.explain
manifest.summary: Explain what a UCT term, indicator or feature IS (“what does ADR mean?”, “explain RSI”, “the difference between an indicator and a condition”), from UCT's own catalog. Changes nothing.
manifest.hints: target = the guide entry. topic = the member's words for what to explain (an indicator, a UCT term or feature). Prefer it for UCT's own indicators and features — its text is UCT's catalog. Use ONLY for "what is / what does / explain / difference" questions; a request to change something is a command — plan it.

manifest.name: guide.show
manifest.summary: SHOW the member where a control is (on Charts, the Screener, Breadth, the Calendar or the Journal): highlight the real control on their screen with a short step-by-step card (Next / Back / Exit). Changes nothing — use it for "where do I…", "show me how to…", "how do I…" questions, never to do the thing.
manifest.hints: target = the guide entry. feature = one of: watchlistCreate (creating a watchlist); canvas (chart background, grid, crosshair and watermark); link (linking charts and widgets); symbol (changing a chart’s symbol); timeframe (changing the timeframe); indicators (adding and configuring an indicator); charts (creating and arranging several charts); watchlists (using watchlists); layouts (saving and switching layouts); hideDrawings (hiding and showing drawings); drawing (basic drawing tools); settings (finding chart settings). Other pages, only there: screenerScreens (screener), screenerColumns (screener), screenerFilters (screener), breadthViews (breadth), breadthTable (breadth), calendarNextReport (calendar), journalNewNote (journal). A request to DO it ("change my chart to weekly") is a command, not this.

manifest.name: stock.dailyBars
manifest.summary: Answer questions about ONE stock's COMPLETED daily sessions from UCT's daily bars: the close (latest, or on a date), one session's open/high/low/close, the change over N sessions, the high and low of a window (a week, a month, N sessions, or dated), the 52-week range, the distance off its 52-week high, or its pullbacks — each as of a date when one is given. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "how did AAPL close yesterday", "NVDA close last Friday", "AAPL high on 2026-10-15", "TSLA range last week", "NVDA 5-day change". Never for today's price (stock.quote).
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol uppercase; measure = lastClose (the close, latest or on `date`) | session (open/high/low/close/volume of ONE day: "high on", "low on", "open on") | change (N sessions) | range (high and low over a window) | range52w | offHigh (below the 52-week high) | pullbacks; sessions = the N of an N-session change or range (weeks × 5), else null; date = the member's date words exactly ("last friday", "yesterday", "oct 15", "2026-10-15", "last week", "last month") or null for the latest; from = a range's start words ("from X to Y": date = Y), else null. "close last Friday" → lastClose + date; "high on Oct 15" → session + date; "range last week" → range + date (sessions null: the week decides); "range over the last 10 sessions" → range + sessions 10.

manifest.name: stock.quote
manifest.summary: Answer what ONE to FIVE stocks are trading at — price, change vs the previous close, the market session (regular, premarket, after hours, overnight, closed) and how fresh the price is — from UCT's market data. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "what's NVDA trading at?", "AMD premarket", "NVDA and AMD after hours".
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbols = the tickers, uppercase. Not for fundamentals (stock.profile), news or "why is it moving".

manifest.name: stock.themes
manifest.summary: Show which of UCT's curated themes are leading or lagging over a period (1d, 1w, 1m, 3m, 1y, ytd): equal-weight theme returns from UCT's Theme Tracker. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "which themes are leading this week?", "worst themes this month".
manifest.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry. period: 1d|1w|1m|3m|1y|ytd (null = 1d); order: leaders|laggards (null = leaders); limit: rows (null = 10, at most 30). Not for one stock's theme membership or for why a theme is moving (research).

manifest.name: chart.describeSetup
manifest.summary: Describe ONE chart's setup from UCT's own daily bars (completed sessions): the close vs the 20- and 50-bar SMA, the 50/200 SMA trend flags, distance from the 52-week high, the last 10 bars' consolidation width, the last session's volume vs its 50-session average, and the indicators on the chart (names only). Daily, or weekly from the same bars. UCT computes and words every figure. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "describe this setup", "what's the setup here", "and on the weekly?", "same for AMD". Descriptive, never a recommendation.

fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema20: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 20-day exponential moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma50: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 50-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma200: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 200-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema9: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 9-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema10: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 10-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.run_sma50_sma200: The 50-day SMA against the 200-day SMA: +1 is a golden cross, -1 a death cross. [f] [g] [h] [i] [j] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema20: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 20-day exponential moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma50: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 50-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma200: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 200-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema9: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 9-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema10: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 10-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.run_sma50_sma200: The 50-day SMA against the 200-day SMA: +1 is a golden cross, -1 a death cross. [f] [g] [h] [i] [j] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema20: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 20-day exponential moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma50: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 50-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma200: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 200-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema9: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 9-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema10: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 10-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.run_sma50_sma200: The 50-day SMA against the 200-day SMA: +1 is a golden cross, -1 a death cross. [f] [g] [h] [i] [j] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema10: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 10-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.run_sma50_sma200: The 50-day SMA against the 200-day SMA: +1 is a golden cross, -1 a death cross. [f] [g] [h] [i] [j] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.

fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear.
